headline: Mostly dry and mild, with light showers Saturday into Sunday before a drier week.
summary: Western Washington is in a mostly quiet stretch. A weak front passed Thursday, and Friday should be clearer and a bit cooler, with fog and low clouds possible early in the morning south of Puget Sound that should clear by afternoon. A storm center (a low-pressure system) moving in from the north on Saturday brings a chance of showers, mostly over the Olympic Peninsula, with only light rain inland. Showers may linger into Sunday, with drier weather returning by afternoon. Saturday mornings will be cold, and frost or a light freeze is possible in mountain valleys. The rest of next week looks mostly dry. Forecasters see early hints of a more active pattern near the end of the month into early November, possibly bringing heavier rain and mountain snow, but that remains uncertain.
